To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
charge-transfer and charge conserving optical transitions at vanium ions in CdTe are analyzed.
the optical spectra of vanadium-doped cadmium telluride crystals can be explained by the presence of three vanadium oxidation states, i.e., V+, V2+, and V3+.

the PL of vanadium-doped cadmium telluride is due to the charge-conservation and charge-transfer transitions of vanadium in various oxidation states, and the positions of the vanadium-related donor and acceptor levels are determined.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the optical properties of vanadium-doped cadmium telluride.
the optical transitions of vanadium in CdTe.
the optical properties of vanadium ions and intrinsic defects in vanadium-dope CdTe.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the optical spectra of vanadium-doped cadmium telluride are dominated by the charge-transfer and chargeconserving transitions of V+ ions.
the V+ and V3+ centers are the only vanadium-related centers in the CdTe lattice that are relevant for the optical spectra.
the optical properties of V-doped CdTe are dominated by transitions of vanadium in various oxidation states.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
vanadium ions in the oxidation states V3+, V2+, and V+ are present in CdTe, and that the PL bands are assigned to internal charge-transfer transitions of the ions in their various charge states.
the PL spectra of V-doped CdTe can be explained by the charge-transfer and charge-transfer transitions of the vanadium ion in various oxidation states.
the V+ ion in its 3d2 configuration is the most stable in the V2+/3+/+ system, and that the V2+ ion is the most stable of the 3d1 ions in the V2+ system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the V3+ and V2+/2+ features are the only vanadium-related features in the optical spectra of vanadium-doped II-VI semiconductors, while the V+ features are absent.
the optical spectra of vanadium-doped II-VI semiconductors are more complex than those previously thought and the presence of charge-transfer transitions has to be considered.
the optical spectra of the vanadium-doped II-VI compound semiconductors can be explained in the context of the Tanabe-Sugana crystal-field model.
